occurrences: p.32 J3 step 5 ('hour ×3 hours'); p.33 J4 step 5 ('2 yards ×36 inches per yard'); p.33 J5 step 5 ('gallon ×5 gallons')
quote: Check: 70 miles per hour ×3 hours = 210 miles.
correction: Check: 70 miles per hour × 3 hours = 210 miles.
why: The multiplication sign has a space before it but none after, so it renders fused to the following number (×3), unlike every other × in the document (e.g. "3 × 70 = 210" two lines above).

quote: because 6/3 = 2 and 2/3 remains. Same mixed number.
correction: because \frac{6}{3} = 2 and \frac{2}{3} remains. Same mixed number. (render 6/3 and 2/3 as stacked fractions to match the rest of the sentence)
why: The same sentence renders 8/3 and 2/3 as stacked fractions and then switches to slash notation for 6/3 and 2/3, so one sentence shows two different fraction notations for the same kind of quantity.

quote: Factor 90 into any pair: 90 = 9 × 10, or better start dividing by small primes.

quote: To flip an inequality means swap the two sides and reverse the symbol (< becomes >, or > becomes <).

why: The word "and" is set in bold mid-sentence, but everywhere else in these Important-words bullets emphasis is italic (e.g. "the endpoint is not included" on p.27) and bold is reserved for section labels, so the bold "and" is an inconsistent emphasis style.

quote: This question asks you to rewrite 7 × a by swapping the order of the two numbers being multiplied.
